themes_detail.label: Encampment surge this week
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK, up 700% from a baseline average of 0.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a rapid deterioration in homelessness visibility or a concentrated cluster in a specific location that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 7 encampment complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.82)
700% spike represents the most acute emerging issue in the dataset by recency
No prior community board or news coverage suggests this is a new or rapidly worsening phenomenon
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: Map the 7 complaints geographically—are they clustered near Coney Island boardwalk, transit hubs, or parks? Interview residents and business owners.
City services angle: Are DSNY, NYPD, or DHS resources allocated to CD313? What's the response timeline?

themes_detail.label: Drinking complaints spike last week
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints jumped to 4 LAST WEEK, a 3100% spike from a baseline average of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks, indicating either a sudden enforcement crackdown or a localized public drinking concentration.
evidence: 4 drinking complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72, severity: high)
Spike is statistically extreme but very recent (last week only), requiring confirmation of whether trend persists
Paired with encampment spike, may indicate related street-level quality-of-life issue
reporting_angles: Enforcement angle: Has NYPD ramped up public drinking enforcement in CD313 over the past 7-10 days? Request precinct data.
Cluster reporting: Which specific parks, beaches, or commercial strips are driving complaints? Interview beat officers.

themes_detail.label: Indoor air quality complaints surge
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints jumped to 8 LAST WEEK, a 276% spike from a baseline average of 2.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting either mold/moisture issues in residential buildings or a new source of contamination affecting multiple units.
evidence: 8 indoor air quality complaints last week vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.34, severity: high)
Spike aligns with broader pattern of heat/hot water complaints (1,023 over 90 days), suggesting building maintenance issues may be systemic
No prior news coverage or community board records indicate unaddressed air quality crisis
reporting_angles: Building maintenance investigation: Focus on older waterfront buildings (Brighton Beach, Coney Island residential areas) with known heating/plumbing issues. Request DOB violation history.
Tenant voice: Interview residents filing complaints—are complaints concentrated in specific buildings? Is there evidence of mold, condensation, or chemical odors?

themes_detail.label: Overgrown trees and vegetation 2 weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints hit 3 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO, a 2300% spike from a baseline average of 0.1 per week, indicating either seasonal growth or deferred maintenance by Parks Department in this waterfront community.
evidence: 3 overgrown tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69, severity: high)
Timing is slightly older than other spikes, making it lower priority than this-week and last-week signals
May reflect seasonal cycle (spring/early summer growth) rather than emerging crisis
reporting_angles: Parks maintenance: Confirm whether NYC Parks has deferred maintenance requests in CD313. Are tree-trimming crews allocated to Coney Island/Brighton Beach?
Quick follow-up: Have complaints subsided in the past week, or is this an ongoing trend? Current ground conditions assessment needed.

themes_detail.label: Street sign removal cluster 3 weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints spiked to 4 THREE WEEKS AGO, a 700% spike from a baseline average of 0.5 per week, suggesting either weather damage, infrastructure degradation, or a specific localized event that warrants wayfinding assessment.
evidence: 4 missing street sign complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.0, severity: high)
Spike is older than this-week and last-week signals, lowering editorial priority
No confirmation whether signs were replaced or cluster has persisted into current week
reporting_angles: Quick verification: Request DOT records on missing sign complaints and repair work in CD313 for the past 3 weeks.
Low-priority follow-up only if trend has persisted into this week.
